claims.text: Grants support exhibitions.
Grants support commissions.
Grants support acquisitions.
Grants support conservation.
Grants support conferences.
Grants support publications.
Grants support long-term research.

Grants are available for exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, commissions, conferences, research, non-commercial publications and the development of collections through acquisitions, conservation, cataloguing and display.
Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators can apply to the Research and Travel category.
Individuals wishing to create, inform, develop or research their own practice are not eligible to apply.
Community project applications will only be considered when the applicant is a non-profit arts organisation.
Henry Moore Grants are available to non-profit organisations.
The maximum grant available for New Projects and Commissions is £20,000.
The maximum grant available for Acquisitions and Collections is £20,000.
The maximum grant available for Conferences, Lectures and Publications is £5,000.
The maximum grant available for Long-Term Research grants is £20,000.
Henry Moore Grants are available to individuals in the Research and Travel category only.
Research and Travel grants are available to sculpture historians, academics and conservators.
Research and Travel grants support research costs, travel, photography and archival access.
Applications for Research and Travel grants cannot be for informing or developing an artist’s own work, and/or professional practice.
The maximum grant available for Research and Travel grants is £2,500.
Grant applications are administered using Flexi-Grant.
Applications are considered four times per year.
Autumn submissions close on 1 September at 23:00.
Projects funded in the Autumn round must start or open to the public no sooner than 1 January 2027.
Winter applications open on 1 November at 9:00.
Winter submissions close on 1 December at 23:00.
Projects funded in the Winter round must start or open to the public no sooner than 1 April 2027.
Spring applications open on 1 February 2027 at 9:00.
Spring submissions close on 1 March 2027 at 23:00.
Projects funded in the Spring round must start or open to the public no sooner than 1 July 2027.
Summer applications open on 1 May 2027 at 9:00.
Summer submissions close on 1 June 2027 at 23:00.
Projects funded in the Summer round must start or open to the public no sooner than 1 October 2027.
Organisations must be registered to apply.
Registration requests must be received one week before the deadline.
The Henry Moore Institute supports researchers through its sculpture research programme.
Research fellowships allow researchers to spend a month using facilities in Leeds.
Research fellowships include accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses.
